encounters.cc: presents to the clinic for a routine follow-up

lines: He presents to the clinic for a routine follow-up
He has been managing his diabetes with metformin and a balanced diet.
He reports no new symptoms and is adherent to his medication.
- Father: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, myocardial infarction at age 62
His blood pressure is 132/86 mmHg, and his body mass index is 30 kg/m^2.
His feet are intact with palpable pulses and no signs of ulceration.
Recent laboratory results are as follows:
- Urinalysis: No glucose, no ketones, no blood
The patient is a 58-year-old male with Type 2 diabetes mellitus of 15 years' duration returning for hypertension management, last seen six months ago for routine diabetes follow-up.
He was diagnosed with hypertension 6 months ago.
Despite adherence to lifestyle modifications including dietary changes and increased physical activity, his blood pressure remains elevated.
His last visit 2 months ago showed a blood pressure of 158/94 mmHg.
He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and hyperlipidemia.
His current medication includes metformin 1000 mg twice daily and atorvastatin 20 mg at bedtime.
- Father: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, myocardial infarction at age 62
Today, his blood pressure is 162/98 mmHg.
His physical examination is unremarkable except for obesity. His BMI is 32 kg/m^2.

encounters.cc: gradually worsening vision over the past year

lines: Gradually worsening vision over the past year

The patient is a 59-year-old male with a 15-year history of type 2 diabetes mellitus who presents for ophthalmologic evaluation following recent internal medicine follow-up for his chronic conditions.
He has not had recent eye examinations and reports that his glasses no longer help him see clearly.
He occasionally notices dark spots drifting in his field of vision, and at night he struggles to distinguish objects in dim light.
There is no headache, jaw pain, or limb weakness, and he has not experienced acute eye pain.
He was diagnosed with diabetes mellitus 15 years ago and admits that his blood glucose levels have often been poorly controlled despite multiple medications.
- Father: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, myocardial infarction at age 62
His blood pressure is 148/92 mmHg, pulse is 78/min, and BMI is 31 kg/m².
Visual fields are constricted bilaterally, and intraocular pressure is normal.
Laboratory evaluation reveals a hemoglobin A1c of 9.6%.

encounters.cc: fatigue, daytime sleepiness, and a recent episode of palpitations

lines: Fatigue, daytime sleepiness, and a recent episode of palpitations
Patient with diabetes and proliferative retinopathy presents with fatigue and daytime sleepiness.
He reports his wife observed him snoring loudly and having periods of apnea during sleep.
He denies chest pain, dizziness, or syncope.
His medications include metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin.
- Father: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, myocardial infarction at age 62
On physical examination, his blood pressure is 145/90 mmHg, heart rate is irregularly irregular at 110 bpm, and BMI is 32 kg/m^2.
Cardiac auscultation reveals an irregular rhythm without murmurs, and lung fields are clear.
An electrocardiogram shows atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response.
Overnight polysomnography is scheduled and demonstrates an apnea-hypopnea index of 22 events per hour.

encounters.cc: presents to the clinic for a follow-up visit with increasing fatigue and shortness of breath on exertion

lines: He presents to the clinic for a follow-up visit with increasing fatigue and shortness of breath on exertion
The patient with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and prior OSA returns for follow-up with increasing fatigue and shortness of breath on exertion over the past 6 months.
He denies chest pain, palpitations, or syncope.
His medications include metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin.
- Father: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, myocardial infarction at age 62
On physical examination, his blood pressure is 138/86 mmHg, heart rate is 78 bpm, and BMI is 32 kg/m^2.
Auscultation of the heart reveals a soft S4 gallop.
The patient is referred for an echocardiogram, which shows left ventricular diastolic dysfunction with preserved ejection fraction.
The patient is concerned about the implications of his condition and asks about the reliability of the echocardiogram findings.

encounters.cc: progressive dyspnea on exertion and fatigue

lines: Progressive dyspnea on exertion and fatigue
The patient returns to the Cardiology clinic for follow-up of his heart failure and longstanding type 2 diabetes mellitus with proliferative retinopathy.
He presents complaining of progressive dyspnea on exertion and fatigue over the past 6 months.
He also reports a recent episode of paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea.
He denies chest pain, palpitations, or syncope.
- Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (diagnosed 2023-07-15)
His medications include metformin, lisinopril, and hydrochlorothiazide.
- Father: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, myocardial infarction at age 62
On physical examination, his blood pressure is 130/85 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute.
Cardiac auscultation reveals an S3 gallop and bibasilar crackles are noted on lung auscultation.
Extremities show 1+ bilateral lower extremity edema.
A subsequent echocardiogram reveals a left ventricular ejection fraction of 30%.
An ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy.

encounters.cc: presents to the clinic for a routine follow-up with worsening fatigue and shortness of breath

lines: He presents to the clinic for a routine follow-up with worsening fatigue and shortness of breath
The patient returns for cardiology follow-up with progression of symptoms evaluated in July 2023 and January 2024.
He complains of increasing fatigue and shortness of breath on exertion over the past 6 months.
He denies chest pain, palpitations, or syncope.
- Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (diagnosed 2023-07-15)
- Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (diagnosed 2024-01-15)
His medications include metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin.
- Father: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, myocardial infarction at age 62
On physical examination, his blood pressure is 142/88 mmHg, heart rate is 78 bpm, and BMI is 32 kg/m^2.
Cardiac examination shows an S4 gallop.
No lower extremity edema is noted.
- Chest X-ray: Mild cardiomegaly with no acute disease
The patient is enrolled in a factorial design study to evaluate the effects of two interventions on heart failure outcomes.
He is randomized to receive either a beta-blocker or a placebo, and either an ACE inhibitor or an ARB.

encounters.cc: progressive shortness of breath, orthopnea, and lower extremity edema

lines: Progressive shortness of breath, orthopnea, and lower extremity edema

The patient with Type 2 diabetes mellitus and heart failure, decompensated three months prior, presents to the emergency department with progressive shortness of breath, orthopnea, and lower extremity edema over the past two weeks.
He reports a 10-pound weight gain during this period.
- Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (diagnosed 2023-07-15)
- Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (diagnosed 2024-01-15)
He takes metformin, lisinopril, and hydrochlorothiazide.
- Father: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, myocardial infarction at age 62
Blood pressure is 150/90 mmHg, heart rate is 102 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 22 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation is 90% on room air
Cardiac auscultation reveals an S3 gallop.
Extremities show 2+ pitting edema up to the mid-shins.
Chest X-ray shows cardiomegaly and pulmonary congestion.
An echocardiogram reveals a left ventricular ejection fraction of 30%.
